title.zh: 卷二十六 唐書2: 武皇本紀下
title.en: Volume 26 Book of Later Tang 2: Wuhuang Annals 2
title.raw: 卷二十六 唐書2: 武皇本紀下 Volume 26 Book of Later Tang 2: Wuhuang Annals 2

sentences.zh: 八月，赫連鐸誘幽州李匡威之眾八萬，寇天成軍，遂攻雲州，營於州北，連亙數里。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Helian Duo induced eighty thousand of Youzhou Li Kuangwei's troops, raided Tiancheng Army, then attacked Yunzhou, encamping north of the prefecture in a line several li long.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Helian Duo won over eighty thousand of Li Kuangwei's Youzhou troops, struck Tiancheng Army, then besieged Yunzhou with camps stretching several li north of the city.

sentences.zh: 武皇潛軍入於雲州，詰旦，出騎軍以擊之，斬獲數萬，李匡威燒營而遁。

translations.literal: Wuhuang secretly entered Yunzhou with troops; at dawn he led cavalry out to attack, beheading and capturing tens of thousands; Li Kuangwei burned his camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang slipped into Yunzhou with his army; at dawn his horsemen fell on them, killing or capturing tens of thousands, and Li Kuangwei burned his camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 十月，邢州李存孝叛，納款於梁，李存信構之也。

translations.literal: Tenth month, Xingzhou's Li Cunxiao rebelled, submitted allegiance to Liang; Li Cunxin had framed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao of Xingzhou rebelled and went over to Liang after Li Cunxin set him up.

sentences.zh: 景福二年春，大舉以伐王鎔，以其通好於李存孝也。

translations.literal: Spring of Jingfu year 2, a great campaign was launched against Wang Rong because he was on good terms with Li Cunxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Jingfu 2 Wuhuang marched in force against Wang Rong for keeping ties with Li Cunxiao.

sentences.zh: 二月，攻天長鎮，旬日不下。

translations.literal: Second month, they attacked Tianchang Fort; for ten days it would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he attacked Tianchang Fort, which held out for ten days.

sentences.zh: 王鎔出師三萬來援，武皇逆戰於叱日嶺下，鎮人敗，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Wang Rong sent thirty thousand men to the relief; Wuhuang met them below Chiri Ridge; the Zhen men were defeated and more than ten thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong sent thirty thousand reinforcements; Wuhuang met them at Chiri Ridge, routed the Zhen army, and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑，軍乏食，脯屍肉而食之。

translations.literal: Famine struck that year; the army lacked food and dried flesh from corpses to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Famine left the army starving; they ate dried flesh from the dead.

sentences.zh: 進軍下井陘，李存孝將兵夜入鎮州，鎮人乞師於汴；

translations.literal: Advancing through Jingxing Pass, Li Cunxiao led troops by night into Zhenzhou; the Zhen men begged Bian for troops;
translations.idiomatic: He pushed down Jingxing Pass; Li Cunxiao stole into Zhenzhou by night while the city called on Bian for aid;

sentences.zh: 汴帥方攻時溥，不暇應之。

translations.literal: The Bian commander was then attacking Shi Pu and had no leisure to respond.
translations.idiomatic: but the Bian commander was busy attacking Shi Pu and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 乃求援於幽州，李匡威率兵赴之，武皇乃班師。

translations.literal: They then sought aid from Youzhou; Li Kuangwei led troops to the rescue, and Wuhuang withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong turned to Youzhou; Li Kuangwei marched to help, and Wuhuang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 七月，武皇討李存孝於邢州，遂攻平山，渡滹水，攻鎮州。

translations.literal: Seventh month, Wuhuang campaigned against Li Cunxiao at Xingzhou, then attacked Pingshan, crossed the Hutuo River, and attacked Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wuhuang attacked Li Cunxiao at Xingzhou, took Pingshan, crossed the Hutuo, and moved on Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 王鎔懼，以帛五十萬犒軍，請修舊好，仍以鎮、冀之師助擊存孝，許之。

translations.literal: Wang Rong was afraid; with five hundred thousand bolts of silk he rewarded the army, asked to renew the old friendship, and still offered Zhen and Ji troops to help strike Cunxiao; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, in terror, sent five hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, sued for peace, and pledged Zhen and Ji troops against Cunxiao; Wuhuang agreed.

sentences.zh: 武皇進圍邢州。

translations.literal: Wuhuang advanced to besiege Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang pressed the siege of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，武皇狩於近郊，獲白兔，有角長三寸。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Wuhuang hunted near the suburbs and caught a white hare with horns three inches long.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he hunted near the capital and took a white hare with three-inch horns.

sentences.zh: 乾寧元年三月，邢州李存孝出城首罪，縶歸太原，轘於市。

translations.literal: Third month of Qianning year 1, Li Cunxiao of Xingzhou came out to confess guilt, was bound and sent to Taiyuan, and was torn apart at the market.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Qianning 1 Li Cunxiao surrendered at Xingzhou, was sent bound to Taiyuan, and executed by dismemberment in the market.

sentences.zh: 邢、洺、磁三州平。

translations.literal: Xing, Mo, and Ci prefectures were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, Mo, and Ci were pacified.

sentences.zh: 武皇表馬師素為邢州節度使。

translations.literal: Wuhuang memorialized Ma Shisu as military commissioner of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Ma Shisu as commissioner of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，鄆州節度使朱瑄為汴軍所攻，遣使來乞師。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the Yanzhou military commissioner Zhu Xuan was attacked by Bian troops and sent envoys begging for troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhu Xuan of Yan was besieged by Bian and asked for help.

sentences.zh: 武皇遣騎將安福順、安福應、安福遷督精騎五百，假道於魏州以應之。

translations.literal: Wuhuang sent the cavalry commanders An Fushun, An Fuying, and An Fuqian with five hundred elite horsemen, passing through Weizhou by leave to answer him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent An Fushun, An Fuying, and An Fuqian with five hundred picked horsemen through Weizhou to his aid.

sentences.zh: 九月，潞州節度使康君立以鴆死。

translations.literal: September, the Luzhou military commissioner Kang Junli died of poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Kang Junli, commissioner of Lu, died of poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 十月，武皇自晉陽率師伐幽州。

translations.literal: October, Wuhuang personally led troops from Jinyang to campaign against Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Wuhuang marched from Jinyang against Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，李匡儔奪據兄位，燕人多不義之，安塞軍戍將劉仁恭挈族歸於武皇，武皇遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Kuangchou had seized his brother's position; many in Yan viewed it as unjust; Liu Rengong, garrison officer of Anse Army, brought his clan to Wuhuang, who treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangchou had ousted his brother, and the Yan people resented him; Liu Rengong, garrison officer at Anse, came over with his clan, and Wuhuang received him warmly.

sentences.zh: 仁恭數進畫於蓋寓，言幽州可取之狀，願得兵一萬，指期平定。

translations.literal: Rengong repeatedly presented plans to Gai Yu on how Youzhou could be taken, asking for ten thousand men and promising to pacify it within a set term.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong urged Gai Yu again and again that ten thousand men could take Youzhou on a fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 武皇方討李存孝於邢州，輟兵數千，欲納仁恭，不利而還。

translations.literal: Wuhuang was then campaigning against Li Cunxiao at Xingzhou; he spared a few thousand men intending to install Rengong, but without success withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: While Wuhuang was still at Xingzhou he diverted a few thousand men for Rengong but had to pull back without gain.

sentences.zh: 匡儔由是驕怠，數犯邊境，武皇怒，故率軍以討之。

translations.literal: Kuangchou thereby grew arrogant, repeatedly raiding the border; Wuhuang was enraged and therefore led troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangchou grew bold and raided the frontier until Wuhuang marched to punish him.

sentences.zh: 是時，雲州吐渾赫連鐸、白義誠並來歸，命皆笞而釋之。

translations.literal: At that time Helian Duo and Bai Yicheng of the Yunzhou Tuyuhun both came in submission; he ordered them all flogged and released.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Duo and Bai Yicheng of Yunzhou Tuyuhun submitted; he had them flogged and let them go.

sentences.zh: 十一月，進攻武州。

translations.literal: November, he advanced to attack Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he attacked Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，攻新州。

translations.literal: On jiayin he attacked Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he assaulted Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，李匡儔命大將率步騎六萬救新州；

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Li Kuangchou ordered a great general to lead sixty thousand foot and horse to relieve Xinzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Li Kuangchou sent a great general with sixty thousand men to relieve Xinzhou;

sentences.zh: 武皇選精甲逆戰，燕軍大敗，斬首萬餘級，生獲將領百餘人，曳練徇於新州城下。

translations.literal: Wuhuang chose crack armor to meet them; the Yan army was utterly defeated, more than ten thousand heads taken and over a hundred officers captured alive, who were dragged in chains before Xinzhou's walls.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang met them with elite armor; the Yan army was crushed, more than ten thousand were killed, and over a hundred officers were paraded in chains before Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 是夜，新州降。

translations.literal: That night Xinzhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhou surrendered that night.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，進攻媯州。

translations.literal: On xinhai he advanced to attack Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he moved on Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 壬子，燕兵復合於居庸關拒戰，武皇命精騎以疲之，令步將李存審由他道擊之，自午至晡，燕軍復敗。

translations.literal: On renzi the Yan troops massed again at Juyong Pass to resist; Wuhuang ordered elite cavalry to weary them and step commander Li Cunshen to strike by another route; from noon to the hour shen the Yan army was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the Yan forces blocked Juyong Pass; Wuhuang tired them with elite horse, while Li Cunshen struck from another road from noon to dusk and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，李匡儔攜其族棄城而遁，將之滄州，隨行輜車，臧獲妓妾甚眾。

translations.literal: On jiayin Li Kuangchou carried his clan and abandoned the city to flee toward Cangzhou; the baggage train was full of servants and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Li Kuangchou fled toward Cangzhou with his clan, his train laden with servants and concubines.

sentences.zh: 滄帥盧彥威利其貨，以兵攻匡儔於景城，殺之，蓋擄其眾。

translations.literal: Cangzhou's commander Lu Yanwei coveted his goods; with troops he attacked Kuangchou at Jingcheng, killed him, and carried off his following.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanwei of Cangzhou wanted his loot, attacked him at Jingcheng, killed him, and seized his train.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，進軍幽州，其守城大將請降，武皇令李存審與劉仁恭入城撫勞，居人如故，市不改肆，封府庫以迎武皇。

translations.literal: On bingchen he advanced to Youzhou; the defending great generals asked to surrender; Wuhuang ordered Li Cunshen and Liu Rengong into the city to reassure the people; inhabitants were as before, markets unchanged, treasuries sealed to welcome Wuhuang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he entered Youzhou; the garrison commanders submitted; Li Cunshen and Liu Rengong pacified the city, business went on as usual, and the treasuries were sealed for Wuhuang's arrival.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年正月，武皇在幽州，命李存審、劉仁恭徇諸屬郡。

translations.literal: First month of Qianning year 2, Wuhuang was at Youzhou and ordered Li Cunshen and Liu Rengong to bring the subordinate prefectures to heel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianning 2, while Wuhuang held Youzhou, he sent Li Cunshen and Liu Rengong to secure the outlying commanderies.

sentences.zh: 二月，以仁恭為權幽州留後，從燕人之請也。

translations.literal: Second month, at the request of the Yan people Rengong was made acting regent of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Yan people had Rengong made acting regent of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 留腹心燕留德等十餘人分典軍政，武皇遂班師，凡駐幽州四十日。

translations.literal: He left trusted men such as Yan Liude, more than ten in all, to run military and civil affairs; Wuhuang then withdrew the army, having stayed at Youzhou forty days in all.
translations.idiomatic: He left Yan Liude and more than ten trusted men to govern and withdrew after forty days at Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，武皇率蕃漢之師自晉陽趨三輔，討鳳翔李茂貞、邠州王行瑜、華州韓建之亂。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Wuhuang led Tartar and Chinese troops from Jinyang toward the Three Capitals to campaign against the rebels Fengxiang's Li Maozhen, Binzhou's Wang Xingyu, and Huazhou's Han Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he rushed from Jinyang with mixed Tartar and Chinese forces into the capital region against Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Wang Xingyu of Bin, and Han Jian of Hua.

sentences.zh: 先是，三帥稱兵向闕，同弱王室，殺害宰輔。

translations.literal: Earlier the three commanders had raised troops toward the court, jointly weakening the royal house and killing chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the three warlords had marched on the capital, weakened the throne, and murdered chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 時河中節度使王重盈卒，重榮之子珂，即武皇之子婿也，權典軍政。

translations.literal: Then the Hezhong military commissioner Wang Chongying died; his son Ke, who was also Wuhuang's son-in-law, acted in charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongying of Hezhong had just died; his son Ke, Wuhuang's son-in-law, held command.

sentences.zh: 其兄珙為陝州節度使，瑤為絳州刺史，與珂爭河中，遂訴於岐、邠、華三鎮，言珂本蒼頭，不當襲位。

translations.literal: His elder brother Gong was commissioner of Shaanxi, Yao prefect of Jiang, and they contested Hezhong with Ke, then appealed to the Feng, Bin, and Hua commands, saying Ke was a bondservant by birth and should not inherit.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Gong of Shaan and Yao of Jiang fought Ke for Hezhong and told Feng, Bin, and Hua that Ke was born a bondsman and unfit to rule.

sentences.zh: 珂亦訴於武皇，武皇上表保薦珂，乞授河中旄鉞，詔可之。

translations.literal: Ke also appealed to Wuhuang; Wuhuang memorialized recommending Ke and begging the Hezhong baton of command; the edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ke appealed to Wuhuang, who memorialized for Ke and asked the Hezhong commission; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 三帥遂以兵入覲，大掠京師，請授王珂同州節度使，王瑤河中節度使，天子亦許之。

translations.literal: The three commanders then led troops to audience at court, greatly plundered the capital, and asked that Ke be made commissioner of Tong and Yao commissioner of Hezhong; the Son of Heaven also granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The three warlords then entered the capital, looted it, and secured an edict making Ke commissioner of Tong and Yao of Hezhong; the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 武皇遂舉兵表三帥之罪，復移檄三鎮，三鎮大懼。

translations.literal: Wuhuang then raised troops memorializing the crimes of the three commanders and also issued proclamations to the three commands; the three commands were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang marched instead, denouncing the three warlords in memorials and proclamations until they were terrified.

sentences.zh: 是月，次絳州，刺史王瑤登陴拒命，武皇攻之，旬日而拔，斬王瑤於軍門，誅其黨千餘人。

translations.literal: That month he halted at Jiang prefecture; prefect Wang Yao manned the walls and defied orders; Wuhuang attacked; in ten days it fell; Wang Yao was beheaded at the army gate and more than a thousand partisans were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That month at Jiangzhou Wang Yao held the walls; Wuhuang took the city in ten days, beheaded Yao before the army, and killed more than a thousand of his faction.

sentences.zh: 七月，次河中，王珂迎謁於路。

translations.literal: Seventh month, he halted at Hezhong; Wang Ke met and welcomed him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he reached Hezhong, where Ke met him on the road.

sentences.zh: 己未，同州節度使王行約棄城奔京師，與左軍兵士劫掠西市，都民大擾。

translations.literal: On jiwei Tongzhou military commissioner Wang Xingyue abandoned the city and fled to the capital; with Left Army soldiers he plundered the Western Market and the capital people were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Wang Xingyue of Tong abandoned his post, fled to Chang'an, and with the Left Army looted the Western Market until the city was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 行約，即行瑜弟也。

translations.literal: Xingyue was Wang Xingyu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyue was the younger brother of Wang Xingyu.

sentences.zh: 庚申，樞密使駱全瓘以武皇之軍將至，請天子幸。

translations.literal: On gengshen Palace Secretariat commissioner Luo Quanzhen, because Wuhuang's army was about to arrive, asked the Son of Heaven to travel.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Luo Quanzhen of the Palace Secretariat, seeing Wuhuang's army approach, urged the emperor to flee.

sentences.zh: 右軍指揮使李繼鵬，茂貞假子也，本姓閻，名珪，與全瓘謀劫天子幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: Right Army commander Li Jipeng, Maozhen's adopted son, original surname Yan, name Gui, with Quanzhen plotted to seize the Son of Heaven and go to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jipeng of the Right Army—Maozhen's adopted son, born Yan Gui—plotted with Quanzhen to drag the emperor to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 左軍指揮使王行實，亦行瑜之弟也，與劉景宣欲劫天子幸邠州。

translations.literal: Left Army commander Wang Xingshi, also Xingyu's younger brother, with Liu Jingxuan meant to seize the Son of Heaven and go to Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingshi of the Left Army—another of Xingyu's brothers—and Liu Jingxuan meant to carry him off to Bin.

sentences.zh: 兩軍相攻，縱火燒內門，煙火蔽天。

translations.literal: The two armies fought each other, set fire to the inner gates, and smoke and flame covered the sky.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies clashed, burned the inner gates, and smoke blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 天子急詔鹽州六都兵士，令追殺亂兵，左右軍退走。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven urgently edicted the Salt Prefecture Six Capital troops to pursue and kill the disorderly soldiers; the Left and Right Armies withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Salt Prefecture Six Capital troops to suppress the mutineers, and both armies fell back.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜、李茂貞聲言自來迎駕，天子懼，出幸南山，駐蹕於莎城。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen claimed they would come in person to welcome the imperial carriage; the Son of Heaven was afraid, went out to the Southern Hills, and halted at Shacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu and Maozhen claimed they would escort the throne in person; the emperor fled south to Shacheng.

sentences.zh: 是夜，熒惑犯心。

translations.literal: That night Mars invaded the Heart constellation.
translations.idiomatic: That night Mars crossed the Heart mansion.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，武皇進收同州，聞天子幸石門，遣判官王瑰奉表奔問，天子遣使賜詔，令與王珂同討邠、鳳。

translations.literal: On renxu Wuhuang advanced to take Tongzhou; hearing the Son of Heaven had gone to Shimen, he sent judge Wang Gui with a memorial to inquire after him; the Son of Heaven sent envoys with edicts ordering joint campaign with Wang Ke against Bin and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu he took Tongzhou; learning the emperor was at Shimen, he sent Wang Gui with a loyal memorial; the court ordered him and Ke to strike Bin and Feng together.

sentences.zh: 時武皇方攻華州，俄聞李茂貞領兵士三萬至盩厔，王行瑜領兵至興平，欲往石門迎駕，乃解華州之圍，進營渭橋。

translations.literal: At that time Wuhuang was attacking Huazhou; presently he heard Li Maozhen had led thirty thousand troops to Zhi and Wang Xingyu's troops had reached Xingping, meaning to go to Shimen to welcome the carriage; he therefore lifted the siege of Hua and advanced to camp at Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: While he besieged Hua he learned Maozhen had thirty thousand men at Zhi and Xingyu was at Xingping, both bound for Shimen; he raised the siege and camped at Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 天子遣延王戒丕、丹王允齎詔，促武皇兵直抵邠、鳳。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent the Prince of Yan Jiepi and the Prince of Dan Yun bearing edicts to urge Wuhuang's troops to press straight to Bin and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Princes Jiepi of Yan and Yun of Dan with edicts urging him straight on Bin and Feng.

sentences.zh: 八月乙酉，供奉官張承業齎詔告諭。

translations.literal: On yiyou of the eighth month attendant Zhang Chengye bore edicts of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the eighth month Zhang Chengye delivered the court's instructions.

sentences.zh: 涇帥張鐺已領步騎三萬於京西北，扼邠、岐之路。

translations.literal: Bin's commander Zhang Dang had already led thirty thousand foot and horse northwest of the capital to block the Bin and Qi roads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dang of Bin already held thirty thousand men northwest of the capital, blocking the roads to Bin and Qi.

sentences.zh: 武皇進營渭北，遣史儼將三千騎往石門扈駕，遣李存信、李存審會鄜延之兵攻行瑜之梨園寨。

translations.literal: Wuhuang advanced to camp north of the Wei; he sent Shi Yan with three thousand horsemen to Shimen to escort the carriage, and sent Li Cunxin and Li Cunshen to join Fuyan troops in attacking Xingyu's Liyuan stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang camped north of the Wei, sent Shi Yan with three thousand horse to escort the emperor at Shimen, and sent Li Cunxin and Li Cunshen with Fuyan forces against Xingyu's Liyuan camp.

sentences.zh: 天子削奪行瑜官爵，以武皇為天下兵馬都招討使，以鄜州李思孝為北面招討使，以涇州張鐺為西南面招討使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven stripped Xingyu of rank and office, made Wuhuang overall commander of all armies, Li Sixiao of Fuzhou northern commander, and Zhang Dang of Binzhou southwestern commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor degraded Xingyu, named Wuhuang commander of all armies, Li Sixiao northern commander, and Zhang Dang southwestern commander.

sentences.zh: 天子又遣延王、丹王賜武皇禦衣及大將茶酒、弓矢，命二王兄事武皇。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again sent the Princes of Yan and Dan to bestow on Wuhuang imperial robes and on great generals tea, wine, bows, and arrows, ordering the two princes to treat Wuhuang as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The princes brought imperial robes for Wuhuang, tea, wine, bows, and arrows for his generals, and were told to honor him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 延王傳天子密旨云：「一昨非卿至此，已為賊庭行酒之人矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan transmitted the Son of Heaven's secret order, saying: "Yesterday had you not come here, we would already be wine-servers in the rebel court.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiepi passed a secret message: "Had you not come yesterday, I would already be pouring wine for the rebels.

sentences.zh: 所慮者二凶締合，卒難翦除，且欲姑息茂貞，令與卿修好，俟梟斬行瑜，更與卿商量。

translations.literal: What is feared is that the two villains will join forces and suddenly be hard to cut down; for now we wish to appease Maozhen and have him make peace with you, waiting until Xingyu is beheaded, then discuss further with you.
translations.idiomatic: The court fears the two rebels will unite and prove hard to destroy; for now we must placate Maozhen and have him treat with you until Xingyu is killed—then we can decide more.

sentences.zh: 」武皇上表，請駕還京。

translations.literal: " Wuhuang memorialized asking that the carriage return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuhuang asked the emperor to return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 令李存節領二千騎於京西北，以防邠賊奔突。

translations.literal: He ordered Li Cunjie to lead two thousand horsemen northwest of the capital to guard against Bin rebels breaking out.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Li Cunjie with two thousand horse northwest of the capital to block any Bin breakout.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，天子還宮，加武皇守太師、中書令、邠寧四面行營都統。

translations.literal: On xinhai the Son of Heaven returned to the palace; Wuhuang was advanced to Guardian Grand Master, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and overall commander of the four-sided Bining campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the emperor re-entered the palace and promoted Wuhuang to Grand Guardian, Imperial Secretary, and chief of the Bining expedition.

sentences.zh: 時王行瑜弟兄固守梨園寨，我師攻之甚急，李茂貞遣兵萬餘來援行瑜，營於龍泉鎮，茂貞自率兵三萬迫咸陽。

translations.literal: Then Wang Xingyu's brothers held firm in the Liyuan stockade; our army pressed the attack fiercely; Li Maozhen sent more than ten thousand troops to relieve Xingyu, encamping at Longquan Fort; Maozhen himself led thirty thousand to press Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu's brothers held Liyuan under heavy assault; Maozhen sent ten thousand reinforcements to Longquan and marched thirty thousand on Xianyang himself.

sentences.zh: 武皇奉請詔茂貞罷兵，兼請削奪茂貞官爵。

translations.literal: Wuhuang memorialized asking that Maozhen halt troops, and also asked that Maozhen be stripped of rank and office.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang asked that Maozhen withdraw and be stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「茂貞勒兵，蓋備非常，尋已發遣歸鎮。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Maozhen arrays troops only to meet the extraordinary; he has already been sent back to his command."
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied that Maozhen had only mobilized in emergency and had already been sent home.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「茂貞已誅李繼鵬、李繼晸，卿可切戒兵甲，無犯土疆。

translations.literal: It also said: "Maozhen has already executed Li Jipeng and Li Jijing; you must strictly restrain your arms and not violate territory."
translations.idiomatic: It added that Maozhen had killed Li Jipeng and Li Jijing and ordered Wuhuang not to cross the border.

sentences.zh: 」武皇請賜河中王珂旌節，三表許之。

translations.literal: Wuhuang asked that the Hezhong baton of command be granted Wang Ke; on the third memorial it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang asked the Hezhong commission for Ke; after three memorials it was granted.

sentences.zh: 又表李罕之為副都統。

translations.literal: He also memorialized Li Hanzhi as deputy overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: He also named Li Hanzhi deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 十月丙戌，李存信於梨園寨北遇賊軍，斬首千餘級，自是賊閉壁不出。

translations.literal: On bingxu of the tenth month Li Cunxin encountered the rebel army north of the Liyuan stockade and beheaded more than a thousand; from this the rebels closed the walls and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu in the tenth month Li Cunxin cut down more than a thousand north of Liyuan; the rebels then held behind their walls.

sentences.zh: 戊子，天子賜武皇內弟子四人，又降朱書御劄，賜魏國夫人陳氏。

translations.literal: On wuzi the Son of Heaven bestowed on Wuhuang four inner palace disciples, and also sent down a vermilion-inscribed imperial missive bestowing on Lady Chen, Madame of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the emperor gave Wuhuang four inner attendants and a vermilion imperial missive honoring Lady Chen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 是月，王行瑜因敗衄之後，閉壁自固，武皇令李罕之晝夜急攻，賊軍乏食，拔營而去。

translations.literal: That month, after defeat Wang Xingyu closed the walls and held firm; Wuhuang ordered Li Hanzhi to press the attack day and night; the rebel army lacked food and abandoned camp and left.
translations.idiomatic: That month, broken in battle, Xingyu held his walls while Li Hanzhi pressed day and night until the rebels, starving, broke camp.

sentences.zh: 李存信與罕之等先伏軍於厄路，俟賊軍之至，縱兵擊之，殺戮萬計。

translations.literal: Li Cunxin with Hanzhi and others had first set troops in ambush on the narrow road; when the rebel army arrived they loosed troops to attack and killed and slaughtered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin and Hanzhi had laid an ambush on the escape road and cut down tens of thousands as the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 是日，收梨園等三寨，生擒行瑜之子知進，並毌丘氏、大將李元福等二百人，送赴闕庭。

translations.literal: That day they took the Liyuan and two other stockades; Xingyu's son Zhijin was captured alive together with the Muqiu lady, great general Li Yuanfu, and two hundred others, all sent to the court.
translations.idiomatic: That day they took Liyuan and two other forts, captured Zhijin, Lady Muqiu, Li Yuanfu, and two hundred more, and sent them to court.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，王行約、王行實燒劫寧州遁走，寧州守將徐景乞降。

translations.literal: On gengyin Wang Xingyue and Wang Xingshi burned and plundered Ningzhou and fled; Ningzhou's defending general Xu Jing begged to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Xingyue and Xingshi sacked Ning and fled; its defender Xu Jing submitted.

sentences.zh: 武皇表蘇文建為邠州節度使，且於寧州為治所。

translations.literal: Wuhuang memorialized Su Wenjian as military commissioner of Binzhou, and moreover made Ningzhou the seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: He made Su Wenjian commissioner of Bin with his seat at Ning.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁巳，收龍泉寨。

translations.literal: On dingsi of the eleventh month they took Longquan stockade.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the eleventh month they took Longquan camp.

sentences.zh: 時行瑜以精甲五千守之，李茂貞出兵來援，為李罕之所敗，邠賊遂棄龍泉寨而去。

translations.literal: Then Xingyu had five thousand crack troops holding it; Li Maozhen sent troops to the relief and was defeated by Li Hanzhi; the Bin rebels then abandoned Longquan stockade and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu had left five thousand elite men there; Maozhen's relief was beaten by Li Hanzhi, and the Bin forces abandoned Longquan.

sentences.zh: 行瑜復入邠州，大軍進逼其城，行瑜登城號哭曰：「行瑜無罪，昨殺南北司大臣，是岐帥將兵脅製主上，請治岐州，行瑜乞束身歸朝。

translations.literal: Xingyu again entered Binzhou; the great army pressed the city; Xingyu mounted the wall and wailed, saying: "Xingyu is without crime; yesterday in killing the northern and southern office great ministers it was the Qi commander who led troops to coerce and control the sovereign—punish Qi prefecture; Xingyu begs to bind himself and return to court."
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu fled into Bin; as the army closed in he wailed from the wall: "I am innocent—the ministers I killed were forced on me by the Fengxiang commander; punish Feng, and I will surrender myself to court."

sentences.zh: 」武皇報曰：「王尚父何恭之甚耶！

translations.literal: Wuhuang replied: "Exalted Father, why so deferential!
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang answered: "Exalted Father, why such humility!

sentences.zh: 仆受命討三賊臣，公其一也。

translations.literal: Your servant received orders to punish three rebel ministers, and you are one of them.
translations.idiomatic: I was ordered to punish three rebel commissioners, and you are one.

sentences.zh: 如能束身歸闕，老夫未敢專命，為公奏取進止。

translations.literal: If you can bind yourself and return to court, this old man dares not decide alone—I will memorialize for the court's decision."
translations.idiomatic: If you surrender, I cannot decide alone—I will ask the throne."

sentences.zh: 」行瑜懼，棄城而遁。

translations.literal: Xingyu was afraid, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, he abandoned Bin and fled.

sentences.zh: 武皇收其城，封府庫，遽以捷聞。

translations.literal: Wuhuang took his city, sealed the treasuries, and at once reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang took the city, sealed the stores, and reported victory at once.

sentences.zh: 既而慶州奏，王行瑜將家屬五百人到州界，為部下所殺，傳首闕下。

translations.literal: Presently Qing prefecture memorialized that Wang Xingyu, with five hundred family members, had reached the prefectural border and was killed by subordinates; his head was sent to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Qing reported that Xingyu, with five hundred kin, was killed by his own men at the border; his head reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 武皇既平行瑜，還軍渭北。

translations.literal: Wuhuang having pacified Xingyu, returned the army to north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Xingyu, Wuhuang withdrew north of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 十二月，武皇營於雲陽，候討鳳翔進止。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Wuhuang encamped at Yunyang, awaiting instructions on the Fengxiang campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he camped at Yunyang, waiting orders against Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 乙未，天子賜武皇為忠貞平難功臣，進封晉王，加實封二百戶。

translations.literal: On yiwei the Son of Heaven bestowed on Wuhuang the merit title Loyal and Upright Pacifier of Rebellion, advanced him to Prince of Jin, and added two hundred households to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the emperor named him Loyal Pacifier of Rebellion, Prince of Jin, with two hundred added fief households.

sentences.zh: 武皇復上表請討李茂貞，天子不允。

translations.literal: Wuhuang again memorialized asking to campaign against Li Maozhen; the Son of Heaven did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again to attack Maozhen; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 武皇私謂詔使曰：「觀主上意，疑仆別有他腸，復何言哉！

translations.literal: Wuhuang privately told the edict envoy: "Seeing the sovereign's intent, he suspects your servant has some other design—what more can be said!
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang told the envoy privately: "The throne suspects I have other designs—what is left to say!

sentences.zh: 但禍不去胎，憂患未已。

translations.literal: Yet calamity does not leave the embryo; worry is not yet over."
translations.idiomatic: But trouble rooted in the womb is not yet cut off."

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「臣統領大軍，不敢徑赴朝覲。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Your servant leads a great army and does not dare go directly to court audience."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote that he dared not bring his army straight to audience.

sentences.zh: 」遂班師。

translations.literal: He then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 乾寧三年正月，汴人大舉以攻兗、鄆，朱瑄、朱瑾再乞師於武皇，假道於魏州，羅宏信許之。

translations.literal: First month of the third year of Qianning, the Bian army launched a major attack on Yan and Yun; Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin again begged Wuhuang for troops; they asked passage through Weizhou, and Luo Hongxin granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianning 3 the Bian forces struck Yan and Yun in strength; Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin again asked Wuhuang for aid and requested a march through Weizhou, which Luo Hongxin allowed.

sentences.zh: 乃令都指揮使李存信將步騎三萬與李承嗣、史儼會軍，以拒汴人。

translations.literal: He then ordered commanding general Li Cunxin to lead thirty thousand foot and horse together with Li Chengsi and Shi Yan to join forces and resist the Bian army.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang ordered Li Cunxin, commander-in-chief, to take thirty thousand mixed infantry and cavalry with Li Chengsi and Shi Yan to meet the Bian advance.

sentences.zh: 存信軍於莘，與朱瑾合勢，頻挫汴軍，汴帥患之，乃間魏人。

translations.literal: Cunxin encamped at Xin, combined strength with Zhu Jin, and repeatedly crushed the Bian army; the Bian commander worried and sowed discord among the Wei men.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin camped at Xin, joined Zhu Jin, and beat the Bian army again and again; the Bian commander grew anxious and turned the Wei troops against him.

sentences.zh: 存信禦兵無法，稍侵魏之芻牧者，宏信乃與汴帥通，出師三萬攻存信軍。

translations.literal: Cunxin disciplined his troops poorly and gradually encroached on Wei fodder and herds; Hongxin then communicated with the Bian commander, sent thirty thousand men, and attacked Cunxin's army.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin could not keep order among his men and began seizing Wei forage and livestock; Hongxin then made common cause with the Bian commander and marched thirty thousand men against Cunxin.

sentences.zh: 存信揭營而退，保於洺州。

translations.literal: Cunxin struck camp and withdrew, holding Ming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin broke camp, fell back, and held Ming prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，武皇大掠相、魏諸邑，攻李固、洹水，殺魏兵萬餘人，進攻魏州。

translations.literal: Third month, Wuhuang greatly plundered the districts of Xiang and Wei, attacked Li Gu and Huanshui, killed more than ten thousand Wei troops, and advanced to attack Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Wuhuang ravaged Xiang and Wei, stormed Li Gu and Huanshui, killed more than ten thousand Wei soldiers, and marched on Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 五月，汴將葛從周、氏叔琮引兵赴援。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the Bian generals Ge Congzhou and Shi Shuzong led troops to relieve.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ge Congzhou and Shi Shuzong of Bian marched to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 六月，李茂貞舉兵犯京師。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Li Maozhen raised troops and invaded the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Li Maozhen took the field against the capital.

sentences.zh: 七月，車駕幸華州。

translations.literal: Seventh month, the imperial carriage went to Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor went to Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 是月，武皇與汴軍戰於洹水之上，鐵林指揮使落落被擒。

translations.literal: That month Wuhuang fought the Bian army above Huanshui; Iron Forest commander Luoluo was captured.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wuhuang met the Bian army on the Huanshui; Luoluo, commander of the Iron Forest Corps, was taken.

sentences.zh: 落落，武皇之長子也。

translations.literal: Luoluo was Wuhuang's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Luoluo was Wuhuang's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 既戰，馬踣於坎，武皇馳騎以救之，其馬亦踣，汴之追兵將及，武皇背射一發而斃，乃退。

translations.literal: After the battle his horse fell into a pit; Wuhuang galloped to save him, and his horse also fell; the Bian pursuers were about to reach him; Wuhuang shot backward one arrow and killed a man, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting his horse went down in a ditch; Wuhuang raced to pull him free and his own mount fell too; as Bian pursuers closed in he shot one man dead over his shoulder and broke off.

sentences.zh: 九月，李存信攻魏之臨清，汴將葛從周等引軍來援，大敗於宗城北。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Li Cunxin attacked Wei's Linqing; the Bian general Ge Congzhou led troops to relieve and was utterly defeated north of Zongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Li Cunxin attacked Linqing in Wei; Ge Congzhou came to relieve it and was routed north of Zongcheng.

sentences.zh: 存信進攻魏州。

translations.literal: Cunxin advanced to attack Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin pressed on to besiege Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，武皇敗魏軍於白龍潭，追擊至觀音門，汴軍救至，乃退。

translations.literal: Tenth month, Wuhuang defeated the Wei army at White Dragon Pool, pursued to Guanyin Gate; Bian relief arrived, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Wuhuang routed the Wei army at White Dragon Pool and chased them to Guanyin Gate until Bian reinforcements came up and he drew back.

sentences.zh: 十一月，武皇征兵於幽、鎮、定三州，將迎駕於華下，幽州劉仁恭托以契丹入寇，俟敵退聽命。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Wuhuang recruited troops from the three prefectures of You, Zhen, and Ding to welcome the carriage below Hua; Youzhou's Liu Rengong pleaded that the Khitan were invading and would obey orders once the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Wuhuang called up troops from You, Zhen, and Ding to escort the emperor back from Hua; Liu Rengong of Youzhou pleaded a Khitan invasion and promised to march once the raiders were gone.

sentences.zh: 乾寧四年正月，汴軍陷兗、鄆，騎將李承嗣、史儼與朱瑾同奔於淮南。

translations.literal: First month of the fourth year of Qianning, the Bian army took Yan and Yun; the cavalry generals Li Chengsi and Shi Yan fled with Zhu Jin to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianning 4 the Bian army captured Yan and Yun; Li Chengsi, Shi Yan, and Zhu Jin fled together to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 三月，陝帥王珙攻河中，王珂來告難；

translations.literal: Third month, the Shaanxi commander Wang Gong attacked Hezhong; Wang Ke came to report distress;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Wang Gong, military commissioner of Shaanxi, attacked Hezhong, and Wang Ke sent word that he was hard pressed;

sentences.zh: 武皇遣李嗣昭率二千騎赴之，破陝軍於猗氏，乃解河中之圍。

translations.literal: Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with two thousand cavalry; he defeated the Shaanxi army at Yishi and lifted the siege of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with two thousand horsemen; Sizhao routed the Shaanxi force at Yishi and broke the siege of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 至是，天子遣延王戒丕至晉陽，傳宣旨於武皇：「朕不取卿言，以及於此，苟非英賢竭力，朕何由再謁廟廷！

translations.literal: By then the Son of Heaven sent Prince Yan Jiepi to Jinyang to proclaim to Wuhuang: "I did not heed your counsel and have come to this pass; but for worthy men's utmost effort, how could I again visit the ancestral temple!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Prince Yan Jiepi to Jinyang with this message for Wuhuang: "Because I would not take your advice I have come to this pass; but for the loyal service of able men, how could I hope to see the ancestral shrines again!

sentences.zh: 在卿表率，予所望也。」

translations.literal: Your exemplary leadership is what I hope for."
translations.idiomatic: I look to you to lead the way."

sentences.zh: 七月，武皇復征兵於幽州，劉仁恭辭旨不遜，武皇以書讓之；

translations.literal: Seventh month, Wuhuang again recruited troops from Youzhou; Liu Rengong's reply was insubordinate; Wuhuang reproved him in a letter;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wuhuang again called on Youzhou for troops; Liu Rengong answered insolently, and Wuhuang rebuked him in writing;

sentences.zh: 仁恭捧書謾罵，抵之於地，仍囚武皇之行人。

translations.literal: Rengong took the letter, cursed it in mockery, threw it to the ground, and still imprisoned Wuhuang's envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong read the letter, reviled it, flung it down, and detained Wuhuang's messenger.

sentences.zh: 八月，大舉以伐仁恭。

translations.literal: Eighth month, he launched a great campaign against Rengong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he marched in force against Rengong.

sentences.zh: 九月，師次蔚州。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the army halted at Yu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army camped at Yu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，晨霧晦暝，占者雲不利深入。

translations.literal: On wuyin morning fog was dark and dim; the diviners said it was unfavorable to advance deeply.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin a thick morning fog settled in; the diviners warned against pushing deep into enemy country.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，攻安塞，俄報「燕將單可及領騎軍至矣。

translations.literal: On xinsi he attacked An'sai; soon came the report, "The Yan general Shan Keji is leading his cavalry here.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he assaulted An'sai; word soon came that "the Yan general Shan Keji is coming with cavalry.

sentences.zh: 」武皇方置酒高會，前鋒又報「賊至矣」！

translations.literal: " Wuhuang was then feasting in high spirits; the vanguard again reported, "The bandits have come!"
translations.idiomatic: " Wuhuang was still at his banquet when the van again cried, "The enemy is here!"

sentences.zh: 武皇曰：「仁恭何在？

translations.literal: Wuhuang said: "Where is Rengong?
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang asked, "Where is Rengong?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「但見可及輩。

translations.literal: " They said: "We see only Keji and his sort.
translations.idiomatic: " They answered, "Only Keji and his men are in sight.

sentences.zh: 」武皇張目怒曰：「可及輩何足為敵！

translations.literal: " Wuhuang glared angrily and said: "Keji and his sort are not fit to be our enemies!
translations.idiomatic: " Wuhuang glared and snapped, "Men like Keji are hardly worth fighting!

sentences.zh: 」仍促令出師。

translations.literal: " Still he urged the army out at once.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet he ordered the troops out immediately.

sentences.zh: 燕軍已擊武皇軍寨，武皇乘醉擊賊，燕軍披靡。

translations.literal: The Yan army had already struck Wuhuang's stockade; Wuhuang, drunk, struck the bandits, and the Yan army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan troops were already hitting his camp; Wuhuang, still drunk, charged the enemy and drove the Yan line back.

sentences.zh: 時步兵望賊而退，為燕軍所乘，大敗於木瓜澗。

translations.literal: Then the foot soldiers, seeing the bandits, withdrew and were exploited by the Yan army; there was a great defeat at Mugua Ravine.
translations.idiomatic: His infantry, however, fell back at sight of the enemy and were cut down; the army was shattered at Mugua Ravine.

sentences.zh: 俄而大風雨震電，燕軍解去，武皇方醒。

translations.literal: Soon great wind, rain, thunder, and lightning came; the Yan army dispersed, and Wuhuang sobered.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden storm of wind, rain, and thunder broke the Yan attack; when it cleared, Wuhuang was sober again.

sentences.zh: 甲午，師次代州，劉仁恭遣使謝罪於武皇，武皇亦以書報之，自此有檄十餘返。

translations.literal: On jiawu the army halted at Dai prefecture; Liu Rengong sent an envoy to apologize to Wuhuang, and Wuhuang also answered by letter; from then more than ten proclamations went back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the army camped at Dai; Liu Rengong sent envoys to apologize, Wuhuang wrote in reply, and more than ten exchanges of letters followed.

sentences.zh: 四月，汴將葛從周寇邢、洺、磁等州，旬日之內，三州連陷。

translations.literal: Fourth month, the Bian general Ge Congzhou raided Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures; within ten days the three prefectures fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Ge Congzhou of Bian overran Xing, Ming, and Ci; all three cities fell within ten days.

sentences.zh: 汴人以葛從周為邢州節度使。

translations.literal: The Bian commander made Ge Congzhou military commissioner of Xing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian commander appointed Ge Congzhou military commissioner of Xing.

sentences.zh: 大將李存信收軍，自馬嶺而旋。

translations.literal: The great general Li Cunxin gathered the army and withdrew from Maling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin gathered his force and pulled back from Maling.

sentences.zh: 八月壬戌，天子自華還宮。

translations.literal: On renxu of the eighth month the Son of Heaven returned from Hua to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in the eighth month the emperor returned from Hua to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時，車駕初復，而欲諸侯輯睦，賜武皇詔，令與汴帥通好。

translations.literal: At that time the carriage had just returned and the court wished the feudatories to live in harmony; an edict was granted to Wuhuang to make peace with the Bian commander.
translations.idiomatic: The court had only just returned to Chang'an and wanted peace among the warlords; Wuhuang was ordered to reconcile with the Bian commander.

sentences.zh: 武皇不欲先下汴帥，乃致書於鎮州王鎔，令導其意。

translations.literal: Wuhuang did not wish to yield first to the Bian commander; he wrote to Wang Rong of Zhen prefecture to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to make the first move toward Bian, Wuhuang wrote Wang Rong of Zhenzhou to sound him out.

sentences.zh: 明年，汴帥遣使奉書幣來修好，武皇亦報之。

translations.literal: The next year the Bian commander sent envoys with letters and gifts to restore good relations; Wuhuang also replied.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Bian commander sent envoys with letters and gifts to reopen relations, and Wuhuang answered in kind.

sentences.zh: 自是使車交馳，朝野相賀。

translations.literal: From then envoys shuttled back and forth, and court and countryside rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys then traveled constantly between the two sides, and the realm breathed easier.

sentences.zh: 九月，武皇遣周德威、李嗣昭率兵三萬出青山口，以迫邢、洺。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with thirty thousand men out Qing Mountain Pass to press Xing and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with thirty thousand men through Qing Mountain Pass against Xing and Ming.

sentences.zh: 十月，遇汴將葛從周於張公橋，既戰，我軍大敗。

translations.literal: Tenth month, they met the Bian general Ge Congzhou at Zhanggong Bridge; after battle our army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they met Ge Congzhou at Zhanggong Bridge and were routed.

sentences.zh: 是月，河中王珂來告急，言王珙引汴軍來寇，武皇遣李嗣昭將兵三千以援之，屯於胡壁堡。

translations.literal: That month Wang Ke of Hezhong reported urgency, saying Wang Gong was leading the Bian army to raid; Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand men to aid him, encamped at Hubi Fort.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wang Ke of Hezhong begged for help against Wang Gong and the Bian army; Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand men to Hubi Fort.

sentences.zh: 汴軍萬餘人來拒戰，嗣昭擊退之。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Bian troops came to resist; Sizhao repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: When more than ten thousand Bian troops came up, Sizhao beat them back.

sentences.zh: 十二月，潞州節度使薛誌勤卒，澤州刺史李罕之以本軍夜入潞州，據城以叛。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Lu prefecture military commissioner Xue Zhiqin died; Ze prefect Li Hanzhi with his army entered Lu at night, seized the city, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xue Zhiqin, military commissioner of Lu, died; Li Hanzhi of Ze led his troops into Lu by night, seized the city, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 罕之報武皇曰：「薛鐵山新死，潞民無主，慮軍城有變，輒專命鎮撫。

translations.literal: Hanzhi reported to Wuhuang: "Xue Tieshan has newly died; the Lu people have no master; fearing unrest in the garrison city, I rashly assumed command to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi wrote Wuhuang: "Xue Tieshan has just died and Lu has no leader; fearing trouble in the city, I took it on myself to restore order.

sentences.zh: 」武皇令人讓之，罕之乃歸於汴。

translations.literal: " Wuhuang sent a man to reprove him; Hanzhi then submitted to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuhuang rebuked him, and Hanzhi then went over to Bian.

sentences.zh: 武皇遣李嗣昭將兵討之，下澤州，收罕之家屬，拘送晉陽。

translations.literal: Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with troops to punish him; he took Ze prefecture, seized Hanzhi's family, and sent them under guard to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao against him; Sizhao took Ze, seized Hanzhi's kin, and sent them as prisoners to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 光化二年春正月，李罕之陷沁州。

translations.literal: Spring, first month of the second year of Guanghua, Li Hanzhi took Qin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Guanghua 2 Li Hanzhi seized Qin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，汴將葛從周、氏叔琮自土門陷承天軍，又陷遼州，進軍榆次。

translations.literal: Third month, the Bian generals Ge Congzhou and Shi Shuzong from Tumen Pass took Chengtian Army, also took Liaozhou, and advanced the army to Yuci.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Ge Congzhou and Shi Shuzong of Bian came through Tumen Pass, took Chengtian Army and Liaozhou, and pushed on to Yuci.

sentences.zh: 武皇令周德威擊之，敗汴軍於洞渦驛，叔琮棄營而遁，德威追擊，出石會關，殺千餘人。

translations.literal: Wuhuang ordered Zhou Dewei to strike them; he defeated the Bian army at Donghuo Post; Shuzong abandoned camp and fled; Dewei pursued through Shihui Pass and killed more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei against them; Dewei routed the Bian force at Donghuo Post, drove Shuzong from his camp, and chased him through Shihui Pass, killing more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 汴人復陷澤州。

translations.literal: The Bian army again took Ze prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian army then recovered Ze prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五月，武皇令都指揮使李君慶將兵收澤、潞，為汴軍所敗而還。

translations.literal: Fifth month, Wuhuang ordered commanding general Li Junqing to lead troops to recover Ze and Lu; he was defeated by the Bian army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wuhuang ordered Li Junqing to retake Ze and Lu; the Bian army beat him back.

sentences.zh: 以李嗣昭為都指揮使，進攻潞州。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao was made commanding general and advanced to attack Lu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao was made commander-in-chief and marched on Lu.

sentences.zh: 八月，嗣昭營於潞州城下，前鋒下澤州。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Sizhao encamped below Lu city; the vanguard took Ze prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Sizhao camped below Lu while his van took Ze.

sentences.zh: 時汴將賀德倫、張歸厚等守潞州。

translations.literal: At that time the Bian generals He Delun and Zhang Guihou and others defended Lu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He Delun, Zhang Guihou, and other Bian generals held Lu.

sentences.zh: 是月，德倫等棄城而遁，潞州平。

translations.literal: That month Delun and the others abandoned the city and fled; Lu prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That month they abandoned Lu and fled; the prefecture was recovered.

sentences.zh: 九月，武皇表汾州刺史孟遷為潞州節度使。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Wuhuang memorialized that Fen prefecture prefect Meng Qian be made military commissioner of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wuhuang asked that Meng Qian, prefect of Fen, be made military commissioner of Lu.

sentences.zh: 光化三年，汴軍大寇河朔，幽州劉仁恭乞師，武皇遣周德威帥五千騎以援之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guanghua the Bian army greatly raided Hebei; Youzhou's Liu Rengong begged for troops; Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei to command five thousand cavalry in relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Guanghua 3 the Bian army swept Hebei; Liu Rengong of Youzhou asked for aid, and Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei with five thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 七月，李嗣昭攻堯山，至內丘，敗汴軍於沙河；

translations.literal: Seventh month, Li Sizhao attacked Yaoshan, reached Neiqiu, and defeated the Bian army at Shahe;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Li Sizhao attacked Yaoshan, reached Neiqiu, and routed the Bian force on the Sha River;

sentences.zh: 進攻洺州，下之。

translations.literal: he advanced to attack Ming prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: he then took Ming prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九月，汴帥自將兵三萬圍洺州，嗣昭棄城而歸，葛從周設伏於青山口，嗣昭之軍不利。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the Bian commander personally led thirty thousand men to besiege Ming; Sizhao abandoned the city and withdrew; Ge Congzhou set an ambush at Qing Mountain Pass, and Sizhao's army suffered.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Bian commander came in person with thirty thousand men to besiege Ming; Sizhao evacuated the city, and Ge Congzhou ambushed him at Qing Mountain Pass.

sentences.zh: 十月，汴人乘勝寇鎮、定，鎮、定懼，皆納賂於汴。

translations.literal: Tenth month, the Bian men, exploiting their victory, raided Zhen and Ding; Zhen and Ding were afraid and both sent bribes to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the victors pressed into Zhen and Ding; both circuits, in fear, paid tribute to Bian.

sentences.zh: 是時，周德威與燕軍劉守光敗汴人二萬於望都，聞定州王郜來奔，乃班師。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Dewei with the Yan army and Liu Shouguang defeated twenty thousand Bian troops at Wangdu; hearing that Dingzhou's Wang Gao was coming in flight, they withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhou Dewei and Liu Shouguang of Yan routed twenty thousand Bian troops at Wangdu; when word came that Wang Gao of Dingzhou was fleeing toward them, they turned back.

sentences.zh: 是月，天子加武皇實封一百戶。

translations.literal: That month the Son of Heaven added a hundred households to Wuhuang's substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor added a hundred households to Wuhuang's substantive fief.

sentences.zh: 遣李嗣昭率步騎三萬攻懷州，下之。

translations.literal: He sent Li Sizhao with thirty thousand foot and horse to attack Huaizhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Sizhao with thirty thousand mixed troops against Huaizhou and took the city.

sentences.zh: 進攻河陽，汴將閻寶率軍來援，嗣昭退保懷州。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Heyang; the Bian general Yan Bao led troops to relieve it; Sizhao withdrew to hold Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao then marched on Heyang; Yan Bao of Bian came to its relief, and Sizhao fell back to defend Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，汴將氏叔琮率兵五萬自太行路寇澤、潞，魏博大將張文恭領軍自新口入，葛從周領兗、鄆之眾自土門入，張歸厚以邢、洺之眾自馬嶺入，定州王處直之眾自飛狐入，侯言以晉、絳之兵自陰地入。

translations.literal: Fourth month, the Bian general Shi Shuzong led fifty thousand men by the Taihang route to raid Ze and Lu; Weibo's great general Zhang Wengong led an army in from Xinkou; Ge Congzhou led the Yan and Yun hosts in from Tumen; Zhang Guihou with the Xing and Ming forces entered from Maling; Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou's host entered from Feihu; Hou Yan with the Jin and Jiang troops entered from Yindi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Shi Shuzong of Bian brought fifty thousand men down the Taihang against Ze and Lu; Zhang Wengong of Weibo entered by Xinkou; Ge Congzhou led the Yan and Yun armies through Tumen; Zhang Guihou came from Maling with the Xing and Ming troops; Wang Chuzhi of Ding entered by Feihu; and Hou Yan led the Jin and Jiang forces through Yindi.

sentences.zh: 氏叔琮、康懷英營於澤州之昂車。

translations.literal: Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying encamped at Angche in Ze prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying camped at Angche in Ze.

sentences.zh: 武皇令李嗣昭將三千騎赴澤州援李存璋，而歸賀德倫。

translations.literal: Wuhuang ordered Li Sizhao with three thousand cavalry to hurry to Ze to aid Li Cunzhang and bring back He Delun.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand horsemen to relieve Ze, aid Li Cunzhang, and recover He Delun.

sentences.zh: 氏叔琮軍至潞州，孟遷開門迎，沁州刺史蔡訓亦以城降於汴，氏叔琮悉其眾趨石會關。

translations.literal: Shi Shuzong's army reached Lu; Meng Qian opened the gate to welcome them; Qin prefecture commissioner Cai Xun also yielded his city to Bian; Shi Shuzong gathered all his forces and pressed toward Shihui Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuzong reached Lu, Meng Qian opened the gates; Cai Xun of Qin surrendered too; and Shuzong drove his whole force toward Shihui Pass.

sentences.zh: 是時，偏將李審建先統兵三千在潞州，亦與孟遷降於汴；

translations.literal: At that time the deputy Li Shenjian had first commanded three thousand men at Lu and also surrendered with Meng Qian to Bian;
translations.idiomatic: The deputy Li Shenjian, who had held Lu with three thousand men, went over to Bian with Meng Qian;

sentences.zh: 及叔琮之入寇也，審建為其鄉導。

translations.literal: when Shuzong invaded, Shenjian served as his native guide.
translations.idiomatic: and when Shuzong invaded he guided the Bian columns.

sentences.zh: 汴人營於洞渦，別將白奉國與鎮州大將石公立自井陘入，陷承天軍。

translations.literal: The Bian army encamped at Donghuo; the separate commander Bai Fengguo with Zhenzhou's great general Shi Gongli entered from Jingxing and took Chengtian Army.
translations.idiomatic: Another Bian column camped at Donghuo while Bai Fengguo and Shi Gongli of Zhen entered by Jingxing and seized Chengtian Army.

sentences.zh: 及攻壽陽，遼州刺史張鄂以城降於汴，都人大恐。

translations.literal: When they attacked Shouyang, Liaozhou prefect Zhang E yielded his city to Bian; the people of the capital were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouyang, Zhang E of Liaozhou surrendered; panic spread through the capital.

sentences.zh: 時霖雨積旬，汴軍屯聚既眾，芻糧不給，復多痢瘧，師人多死。

translations.literal: Rain then fell for more than ten days in succession; the Bian army was massed in great numbers, fodder could not be supplied, and dysentery and malaria were widespread; many soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell for ten days straight; the Bian host was huge, supplies ran out, and dysentery and fever killed many men.

sentences.zh: 時大將李嗣昭、李嗣源每夜率驍騎突營掩殺，敵眾恐懼。

translations.literal: Then the great generals Li Sizhao and Li Siyuan each night led elite cavalry to raid the camps and kill; the enemy masses were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao and Li Siyuan then led night raids with picked cavalry, and the Bian camps lived in dread.

sentences.zh: 五月，汴軍皆退。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the Bian army all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the entire Bian force pulled back.

sentences.zh: 氏叔琮軍出石會，周德威、李嗣昭以精騎五千躡之，殺戮萬計。

translations.literal: As Shi Shuzong's army came out through Shihui, Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with five thousand elite cavalry followed them and killed untold numbers.
translations.idiomatic: As Shuzong withdrew through Shihui, Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao followed with five thousand elite horsemen and cut down countless men.

sentences.zh: 初，汴軍之將入寇也，汾州刺史李瑭據城叛，以連汴人，至是武皇令李嗣昭、李存審將兵討之。

translations.literal: When the Bian army was first about to invade, Fen prefecture prefect Li Tang had held his city and rebelled to join the Bian men; now Wuhuang ordered Li Sizhao and Li Cunzhen to lead troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the invasion Li Tang of Fen had rebelled and sided with Bian; Wuhuang now sent Li Sizhao and Li Cunzhen against him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，並、汾饑，粟暴貴，人多附瑭為亂，嗣昭悉力攻城，三日而拔，擒李瑭等斬於晉陽市。

translations.literal: That year Bing and Fen suffered famine; grain was extremely dear; many people joined Tang in rebellion; Sizhao exerted all his strength in attacking the city; in three days it fell; Li Tang and the others were seized and beheaded in the Jinyang market.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped Bing and Fen that year and grain soared in price; crowds rallied to Li Tang; Sizhao stormed the city in three days, took Li Tang, and executed him in the Jinyang market.

sentences.zh: 氏叔琮既旋軍，過潞州，擄孟遷以歸。

translations.literal: Shi Shuzong, having rotated his army, passed Lu prefecture and carried off Meng Qian on his return.
translations.idiomatic: On the homeward march Shuzong passed through Lu and carried Meng Qian away.

sentences.zh: 汴帥以丁會為潞州節度使。

translations.literal: The Bian commander made Ding Hui military commissioner of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian commander appointed Ding Hui military commissioner of Lu.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣李嗣昭、周德威將兵出陰地，攻慈、隰二郡，隰州刺史唐禮、慈州刺史張瑰並以城來降。

translations.literal: Sixth month, he sent Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei with troops out Yindi to attack the two prefectures of Ci and Xi; Xi prefect Tang Li and Ci prefect Zhang Gui both yielded their cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he sent Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei from Yindi against Ci and Xi; Tang Li of Xi and Zhang Gui of Ci both surrendered.

sentences.zh: 武皇以汴寇方盛，難以兵服，佯降心以緩其謀，乃遣牙將張特持幣馬書檄以諭之，陳當時利害，請復舊好。

translations.literal: Wuhuang, because the Bian raiders were flourishing and hard to subdue by force, feigned submission to slow their plans; he sent tooth officer Zhang Te with gifts, horses, letters, and proclamations to instruct them, set out the advantages and harms of the moment, and asked to restore the old good relations.
translations.idiomatic: With Bian power at its height and victory beyond reach, Wuhuang pretended to yield and sent Zhang Te with gifts, horses, and letters explaining the stakes and asking for peace.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬子，汴帥營於渭濱。

translations.literal: On renzi of the eleventh month the Bian commander encamped on the Wei shore.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi in the eleventh month the Bian commander camped on the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，天子出幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: On jiayin the Son of Heaven went out to favor Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the emperor went to Fengxiang.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《新唐書》：帝如鳳翔，李茂貞、韓全誨請召克用入衛，克用間道遣使者奔問，並詒書全忠，勸還汴，全忠不答。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: When the emperor went to Fengxiang, Li Maozhen and Han Quanhui asked that Li Keyong be summoned to guard the capital; Keyong by a secret route sent envoys to rush inquiry, and also wrote deceitfully to Quanzhong urging him to return to Bian; Quanzhong did not reply.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Book of Tang》 records that when the emperor went to Fengxiang, Li Maozhen and Han Quanhui urged summoning Li Keyong to guard the court; Keyong sent envoys by a hidden route to inquire after him and also wrote Zhu Quanzhong urging him back to Bian, but Quanzhong made no answer.)〉

sentences.zh: 武皇遣李嗣昭率兵三千自沁州趨平陽，遇汴軍於晉州北，斬首五百級。

translations.literal: Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand men from Qin prefecture to hurry to Pingyang; they met the Bian army north of Jin prefecture and beheaded five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand men from Qin to Pingyang; north of Jin prefecture they met the Bian army and took five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 天復二年二月，李嗣昭、周德威領大軍自慈、隰進攻晉、絳，營於蒲縣。

translations.literal: Second month of the second year of Tianfu, Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei led the great army from Ci and Xi to attack Jin and Jiang and encamped at Pu county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianfu 2 Li Sizhao and Zhou Dewei marched from Ci and Xi against Jin and Jiang and camped at Pu county.

sentences.zh: 乙未，汴將朱友寧、氏叔琮將兵十萬，營於蒲縣之南。

translations.literal: On yiwei the Bian generals Zhu Youning and Shi Shuzong led a hundred thousand men and encamped south of Pu county.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Zhu Youning and Shi Shuzong of Bian brought a hundred thousand men and camped south of Pu.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，汴帥自領軍至晉州，德威之軍大恐。

translations.literal: On yisi the Bian commander personally led the army to Jin prefecture; Dewei's army was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi the Bian commander came in person to Jin prefecture, and Dewei's men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 三月丁巳，有虹貫德威之營。

translations.literal: On dingsi of the third month a rainbow crossed Dewei's camp.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the third month a rainbow arched over Dewei's camp.

sentences.zh: 戊午，氏叔琮率軍來戰，德威逆擊，為汴人所敗，兵仗、輜車委棄殆盡。

translations.literal: On wuwu Shi Shuzong led the army to battle; Dewei met the attack and was defeated by the Bian men; weapons and baggage carts were abandoned nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Shi Shuzong gave battle; Dewei met him and was routed; arms and wagons were left behind in heaps.

sentences.zh: 朱友寧長驅至汾州，慈、隰二州復為汴人所據。

translations.literal: Zhu Youning drove on to Fen prefecture; the two prefectures of Ci and Xi were again held by the Bian men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youning pressed on to Fen, and Ci and Xi fell again to Bian.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，汴軍營於晉陽之西北，攻城西門，周德威、李嗣昭緣山保其餘眾而旋。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Bian troops camped northwest of Jinyang and attacked the west gate; Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao led the remnant force along the hills to safety and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day Bian forces camped northwest of Jinyang and assaulted the west gate; Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao took the survivors along the hills and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 武皇驅丁壯登陴拒守，汴軍攻城日急；

translations.literal: Wuhuang drove the able-bodied to the ramparts to resist; the Bian assault grew fiercer day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang pressed every able man onto the walls; the Bian attack tightened day by day.

sentences.zh: 武皇召李嗣昭、周德威等謀將出奔雲州，嗣昭以為不可。

translations.literal: Wuhuang summoned Li Sizhao, Zhou Dewei, and others to plan flight to Yunzhou; Sizhao said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang called Li Sizhao, Zhou Dewei, and the rest to plan an escape to Yunzhou; Sizhao said they must not.

sentences.zh: 李存信堅請且入北蕃，續圖進取，嗣昭等固爭之，太妃劉氏亦極言於內，乃止。

translations.literal: Li Cunxin urgently begged to enter the northern barbarians for the time being and plot advance later; Sizhao and others argued firmly against it, and Grand Consort Liu also spoke strongly within, and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin pressed to withdraw into the northern tribes and strike again later; Sizhao and the others argued him down, Grand Consort Liu spoke fiercely within, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 居數日，亡散之士復集，軍城稍安。

translations.literal: After several days scattered troops reassembled and the fortress grew somewhat calm.
translations.idiomatic: Within days scattered men came back and the garrison steadied.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭與李嗣源夜入汴軍，斬將搴旗，敵人扞禦不暇，自相驚擾。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao and Li Siyuan entered the Bian camp by night, beheaded generals and seized banners; the enemy had no leisure to defend and alarmed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao and Li Siyuan stole into the Bian camp at night, took officers and flags, and threw the enemy into panic before they could rally.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，朱友寧燒營而遁，周德威追至白壁關，俘斬萬計，因收復慈、隰、汾等三州。

translations.literal: On dingmao Zhu Youning burned camp and fled; Zhou Dewei pursued to Bai Bi Pass, captured and killed by the tens of thousands, and recovered Ci, Xi, and Fen.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Zhu Youning burned his camp and fled; Zhou Dewei chased him to Bai Bi Pass, killed or captured tens of thousands, and took back Ci, Xi, and Fen.

sentences.zh: 天復三年正月，天子自鳳翔歸京。

translations.literal: First month of Tianfu 3, the Son of Heaven returned from Fengxiang to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianfu 3 the emperor came back from Fengxiang to the capital.

sentences.zh: 五月，雲州都將王敬暉殺刺史劉再立，以城歸於劉仁恭。

translations.literal: Fifth month, Yunzhou commandant Wang Jinghui killed prefect Liu Zaili and yielded the city to Liu Rengong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wang Jinghui, commandant of Yunzhou, killed Prefect Liu Zaili and gave the city to Liu Rengong.

sentences.zh: 武皇遣李嗣昭討之，仁恭遣將以兵五萬來援雲州，嗣昭退保樂安，燕人擄敬暉，棄城而去。

translations.literal: Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao against him; Rengong sent generals with fifty thousand troops to relieve Yunzhou; Sizhao withdrew to Le'an; the Yan men carried off Jinghui and abandoned the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao to punish him; Rengong sent fifty thousand men to save Yunzhou; Sizhao fell back to Le'an; the Yan troops seized Jinghui and left the city.

sentences.zh: 武皇怒，笞嗣昭及李存審而削其官。

translations.literal: Wuhuang in anger flogged Sizhao and Li Cunshen and stripped their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang in a rage had Sizhao and Li Cunshen beaten and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 是時，親軍萬眾皆邊部人，動違紀律，人甚苦之，左右或以為言。

translations.literal: At that time the personal army of ten thousand were all border men and often broke discipline; the people suffered greatly, and attendants sometimes spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: His personal army of ten thousand were all frontier men and often broke discipline; the people suffered, and his attendants sometimes complained.

sentences.zh: 武皇曰：「此輩膽略過人，數十年從吾征伐，比年以來，國藏空竭，諸軍之家賣馬自給。

translations.literal: Wuhuang said: "These men surpass others in daring; for decades they have followed me in campaigns. In recent years the state treasury has been emptied and soldiers' families sell horses to supply themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang said, "These men are bolder than any others; they have fought with me for decades. Lately the treasury is empty and every household sells horses to live.

sentences.zh: 今四方諸侯皆懸重賞以募勇士，吾若束之以法，急則棄吾，吾安能獨保此乎！

translations.literal: Now the feudal lords everywhere hang heavy rewards to recruit bold men. If I bind them by law, when pressed they will abandon me—how can I alone keep this?
translations.idiomatic: Every lord in the land now offers rich pay for warriors. If I tighten the law on them, they will leave me in a crisis—how could I hold this alone?

sentences.zh: 俟時開運泰，吾固自能處置矣。」

translations.literal: When the time opens and fortune is peaceful I can surely deal with them myself."
translations.idiomatic: When fortune turns and the realm is calm, I can settle them myself."

sentences.zh: 天祐二年春，契丹安巴堅始盛，武皇召之，安巴堅領部族三十萬至雲州，與武皇會於雲州之東，握手甚歡，結為兄弟，旬日而去，留馬千匹，牛羊萬計，期以冬初大舉渡河。

translations.literal: Spring of Tianyou 2, the Khitan Abaoji first rose to power; Wuhuang summoned him; Abaoji led three hundred thousand of his tribes to Yunzhou and met Wuhuang east of Yunzhou; they clasped hands with great joy and became sworn brothers; after ten days he departed, leaving a thousand horses and tens of thousands of cattle and sheep, agreeing on a great crossing of the river in early winter.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Tianyou 2 the Khitan leader Abaoji was rising; Wuhuang called him in. Abaoji brought three hundred thousand tribesmen to Yunzhou and met Wuhuang east of the city; they clasped hands, swore brotherhood, and parted after ten days, leaving a thousand horses and countless herds and promising a great river crossing in early winter.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年正月，魏博既殺牙軍，魏將史仁遇據高唐以叛，遣人乞師於武皇，武皇遣李嗣昭率三千騎攻邢州以應之，遇汴將牛存節、張筠於青山口，嗣昭不利而還。

translations.literal: First month of Tianyou 3, after Weibo killed the yajun troops, Wei general Shi Renyu held Gaotang in rebellion and sent men begging troops from Wuhuang; Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand cavalry to attack Xingzhou in support; they met Bian generals Niu Cunjie and Zhang Yun at Qingshan Pass; Sizhao fared ill and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianyou 3, after Weibo slaughtered the yajun, Wei officer Shi Renyu seized Gaotang and asked Wuhuang for aid. Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand horse against Xingzhou; at Qingshan Pass he met Niu Cunjie and Zhang Yun of Bian, fared badly, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 九月，汴帥親率兵攻滄州，幽州劉仁恭遣使來乞師，武皇乃征兵於仁恭，將攻潞州，以解滄州之圍。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the Bian commander-in-chief personally led troops to attack Cangzhou; Youzhou's Liu Rengong sent envoys begging troops; Wuhuang then requisitioned troops from Rengong intending to attack Lu Prefecture to relieve the siege of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Bian commander marched on Cangzhou in person; Liu Rengong of Youzhou sent envoys asking for help. Wuhuang then drafted Rengong's troops for an attack on Lu Prefecture to lift the siege of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁恭遣掌書記馬鬱、都指揮使李溥等將兵三萬，會於晉陽，武皇遣周德威、李嗣昭合燕軍以攻澤、潞。

translations.literal: Rengong sent chief secretary Ma Yu, chief commander Li Pu, and others with thirty thousand troops to assemble at Jinyang; Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with Yan troops to attack Ze and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong sent his secretary Ma Yu and commander Li Pu with thirty thousand men to Jinyang; Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with the Yan army against Ze and Lu.

sentences.zh: 十二月，潞州節度使丁會開門迎降，命李嗣昭為潞州節度使，以丁會歸於晉陽。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, Lu military commissioner Ding Hui opened the gate and surrendered; Li Sizhao was made military commissioner of Lu; Ding Hui was brought to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Ding Hui, military commissioner of Lu, opened the gates and submitted; Li Sizhao was made commissioner of Lu and Ding Hui was sent to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 天祐四年正月甲申，汴帥聞潞州失守，自滄州燒營而遁。

translations.literal: On jiashen, first month of Tianyou 4, the Bian commander heard Lu had fallen, burned camp at Cangzhou, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the first month of Tianyou 4 the Bian commander learned that Lu had fallen, burned his camp at Cangzhou, and fled.

sentences.zh: 四月，天子禪位於汴帥，奉天子為濟陰王。

translations.literal: Fourth month, the Son of Heaven abdicated to the Bian commander-in-chief and enfeoffed the Son of Heaven as Prince of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the emperor abdicated to the Bian commander and was given the title Prince of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 改元為開平，國號大梁。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Kaiping and the state name to Great Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The era became Kaiping and the state was called Great Liang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，四川王建遣使至，勸武皇各王一方，俟破賊之後，訪唐朝宗室以嗣帝位，然後各歸藩守。

translations.literal: That year Wang Jian of Shu sent envoys urging Wuhuang each to be king in his region; after destroying the bandits, to seek a Tang imperial clansman to succeed the throne, then each return to guard his fief.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Jian of Shu sent envoys urging Wuhuang to declare himself king in his own territory; after the rebels were crushed they would find a Tang clansman for the throne and each return to his post.

sentences.zh: 武皇不從，以書報之曰：

translations.literal: Wuhuang did not comply and replied by letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wuhuang refused and answered in a letter:

sentences.zh: 竊念本朝屯否，巨業淪胥，攀鼎駕以長違，撫彤弓而自咎，默默終占，悠悠彼蒼，生此厲階，永為痛毒，視橫流而莫救，徒誓楫以興言。

translations.literal: I secretly reflect that our dynasty suffers obstruction, its great enterprise sunk; clinging to the imperial carriage yet long parted, stroking the red bow yet blaming myself—silent divination to the end, the distant blue above, this stair of ruin born, forever pain; watching the flood yet unable to save, only vowing the oar to speak out.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that our house is blocked and its great work lost; I reach for the imperial carriage yet am far from it, touch the red bow and blame myself—silent augury, heaven above, this curse upon us, endless pain; I see the flood and cannot save it, and can only swear by the paddle to act.

sentences.zh: 別捧函題，過垂獎諭，省覽周既，駭惕異常。

translations.literal: You separately sent a sealed letter with excessive praise and encouragement; when I read it through I was struck with extraordinary fear.
translations.idiomatic: You sent another letter with lavish praise; when I read it through I was deeply shaken.

sentences.zh: 淚下沾衿，倍鬱申胥之素；

translations.literal: Tears wet my collar, redoubling Shen Xu's old grief;
translations.idiomatic: Tears soaked my robe, as when Shen Xu wept for his state;

sentences.zh: 汗流浹背，如聞蔣濟之言。

translations.literal: sweat ran down my back, as if hearing Jiang Ji's words.
translations.idiomatic: sweat ran down my back, as if Jiang Ji were rebuking me.

sentences.zh: 仆經事兩朝，受恩三代，位叨將相，籍係宗枝，賜鈇鉞以專征，征苞茅而問罪。

translations.literal: Your servant served two dynasties and received grace through three reigns, held rank as general and minister, and was listed among the imperial clan; I was given axe and halberd for independent campaigns and sent with the feudal gift to punish crime.
translations.idiomatic: I have served two courts and three emperors, held the rank of general and minister, and stand in the imperial clan roll; I was given the axe to campaign at will and charged to punish rebels in the king's name.

sentences.zh: 鏖兵校戰，二十餘年，竟未能斬新莽之頭顱，斷蚩尤之肩髀，以至廟朝顛覆，豺虎縱橫。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years I fought in pitched battle yet never cut off Xin Mang's head or severed Chiyou's shoulder, until the court was overturned and wolves and tigers ran wild.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years I fought in the field yet never struck down the usurper or the rebel, until the dynasty fell and beasts ruled the land.

sentences.zh: 且授任分憂，叨榮冒寵，龜玉毀櫝，誰之咎歟！

translations.literal: Yet I was entrusted with office and shared the realm's cares, favored with honor and grace—the jade tortoise broken in its case: whose fault is that!
translations.idiomatic: Yet I was given office and trust, showered with honors—and the jade in its case was shattered. Whose fault is that?

sentences.zh: 俯閱指陳，不勝慚恧。

translations.literal: Bowing to read your pointed counsel, I cannot bear the shame.
translations.idiomatic: Reading your frank advice, I am overcome with shame.

sentences.zh: 然則君臣無常位，陵谷有變遷，或箠塞長河，泥封函谷，時移事改，理有萬殊。

translations.literal: Yet lord and minister have no fixed place, hills and valleys shift; sometimes the Yellow River is dammed and Hangu sealed with mud—times change and affairs alter, and reason has ten thousand forms.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lord and subject do not keep one place forever, and fortune shifts like hills and valleys; rivers are dammed and passes sealed—times change, and principle takes countless forms.

sentences.zh: 即如周末虎爭，魏初鼎據。

translations.literal: So at the end of Zhou tigers contended, and at the start of Wei the tripod was seized.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhou, rivals fought like tigers; at the rise of Wei, men seized the tripod.

sentences.zh: 孫權父子，不顯授於漢恩，劉備君臣，自微興於涿郡。

translations.literal: Sun Quan and his son owed no obvious grant of Han favor; Liu Bei and his ministers rose on their own from Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan and his son owed Han little; Liu Bei and his ministers raised themselves from Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 得之不謝於家世，失之無損於功名，適當逐鹿之秋，何惜華蟲之服。

translations.literal: Gaining the realm owed nothing to family standing; losing it did not harm their fame—this was the season of contending for the deer; why cling to court robes?
translations.idiomatic: Winning the realm did not depend on pedigree; losing it did not stain their names—it was the season of chasing the deer, and court dress meant little.

sentences.zh: 惟仆累朝席寵，奕世輸忠，忝佩訓詞，粗存家法。

translations.literal: Only your servant has enjoyed favor through many reigns and given loyalty through generations; I am shamed to wear your instruction yet still keep the family law.
translations.idiomatic: I alone have been favored through many reigns and loyal through generations; I am unworthy of your counsel, yet I still keep my house's rule.

sentences.zh: 善博奕者惟先守道，治蹊田者不可奪牛。

translations.literal: A good player of chess first keeps the Way; one who tends the border field must not seize another's ox.
translations.idiomatic: A good chess player keeps the rules first; a man who tends his own field must not take another's ox.

sentences.zh: 誓於此生，靡敢失節，仰憑廟勝，早殄寇讎。

translations.literal: I swear in this life never to break faith, relying on the ancestral temple's victory to destroy the foe soon.
translations.idiomatic: I swear never to break faith in this life and trust the ancestral shrine's blessing to destroy the enemy soon.

sentences.zh: 如其事與願違，則共臧洪遊於地下，亦無恨矣。

translations.literal: If affairs go against my wish, then to wander underground with Zang Hong would be no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If heaven wills otherwise, I would rather keep Zang Hong company in the grave and feel no regret.

sentences.zh: 惟公社稷元勳，嵩、衡降祉，鎮九州之上地，負一代之鴻才，合於此時，自求多福。
